docs.text:
Environment variable Default Meaning AGENTIR_HARBOR_BACKEND remote_vllm_tier1 Default backend; a trial kwarg can override it AGENTIR_HARBOR_TIER1_ENDPOINT Trial endpoint Explicit remote endpoint override AGENTIR_HARBOR_TIER1_API_KEY Unset Remote authentication AGENTIR_HARBOR_TIER1_EXPECTED_VERSION 0.24.0 Expected server version AGENTIR_HARBOR_MAX_INFLIGHT 32 Engine request concurrency AGENTIR_HARBOR_MAX_TOKENS 1024 Generation budget per assistant turn AGENTIR_HARBOR_MAX_CALLS 8 Speculative call-slot bound per turn AGENTIR_HARBOR_TEMPERATURE 0 Sampling temperature AGENTIR_HARBOR_INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SEC 1800 Tool-loop timeout AGENTIR_HARBOR_BRIDGE_GRACE_SEC 15 Additional shell-bridge cancellation grace AGENTIR_HARBOR_OUTPUT_CHAR_LIMIT 65536 Prompt limit for each output stream AGENTIR_HARBOR_SPEC_WINDOW 2 Speculative guard depth AGENTIR_HARBOR_MAX_SPEC_INFLIGHT 8 Speculative concurrency budget AGENTIR_HARBOR_RUN_SEED 20260708 Runtime seed AGENTIR_HARBOR_ENGINE_ARGS {} JSON vLLM arguments for local mode only AGENTIR_HARBOR_DEVICES Unset GPU visibility for local mode only AGENTIR_HARBOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT Built in Terminal-agent system prompt

Consult runner.py for validation and the complete effective configuration. For example, an empty expected-version setting disables that version pin; it does not remove the certificate contract.

docs.title: Supply a custom runner
docs.text:
Set runner_import_path to an asynchronous callable with this contract:

(RunnerRequest, Callable[[ShellRequest], Awaitable[ShellObservation]])
    -> Awaitable[RunnerResult]

The adapter still owns environment execution and trajectory persistence. The injected runner owns inference and the tool loop. Types live in agentir.integrations.harbor.protocol and are re-exported by the integration package.

docs.title: Separate latency from throughput
docs.text:
Use one concurrent trial for a task-latency study, and a separately declared higher-concurrency profile for throughput and KV-cache pressure. Do not combine them into a single latency claim. Formal experiment scripts require their locked manifests and resource provenance; see the experiment archive.

The repository also includes a cluster-specific Singularity wrapper in scripts/hephaestus-bin. It strips Harbor's exact --fakeroot argument for the documented hephaestus environment. It is not part of the general Harbor setup.

Source: agent.py, protocol.py, and integration tests.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
This reference covers the supported root exports in agentir.__all__ for 1.3.0. Signatures below emphasize public arguments; types and adapter-specific details live in the linked source modules. Begin with core concepts for the programming model.

The functions are also available through the agentir.api module. agentir.__version__ reports the package version.

docs.title: lit(s)
docs.text: Create a Seq from a string or token-ID tuple, according to the runtime wire. The literal belongs to the current tracing context.

docs.title: cat(*xs) and fmt(template, **parts)
docs.text:
Compose symbolic prompt states. cat preserves producer and observation segments and canonicalizes adjacent literals. fmt supports named composition without automatically converting every handle into a string.

Composition supports at most one independent unresolved choice. Combining independent choices into a Cartesian product is not implemented.

docs.title: infer(x, *, model="main", logprobs=False, hint=0.0, **params)
docs.text:
Register one continuation. A normal result is a Seq containing its input state and generated output. An unresolved Choice is hoisted into guarded per-member continuations. A Val holding a handle introduces a materialization barrier.

params are the validated sampling parameters. Request log probabilities with logprobs=True. hint is scheduling advice, not a score used to select the output.

With tools=registry, this function runs the autonomous tool loop. Its options include max_turns=8, optional max_calls, timeout, and system. The tool loop defaults to eight call slots, a 600-second timeout, 512 output tokens per turn, and temperature zero when not overridden. It returns the final assistant-turn Seq and requires the token wire.

projection= accepts a prepared streamed projection for advanced custom tool control. It conflicts with autonomous tools= mode. The _stream_projection argument is internal.

docs.title: expand(x, k, *, model="main", logprobs=False, hint=0.0, **params)
docs.text: Register k sampling lanes from a shared input. Each lane receives a distinct draw identity. Returns a list of handles; physical prefix reuse depends on the engine cache.

docs.title: text(x) and out_text(x)
docs.text: Return Val[str] for the complete prompt state or the generated tail, respectively. A selected Choice is resolved under its publication conditions when forced.

docs.title: logprobs_of(x) and top_logprobs_of(x)
docs.text: Return asynchronous per-token log-probability observations. The producer must have been created with the required log-probability observation mode and top-k setting. These functions cannot retroactively request engine observations.

docs.title: op(f, *args, pure=False, label="", after=None)
docs.text:
Run a Python function when its inputs are available and its effect conditions permit it. Return a Val. The default fences effects until commitment; pure=True declares replayable computation suitable for speculative execution.

label identifies the operation in diagnostics. after adds predecessor ordering. Keep expensive blocking work out of event-loop callbacks; op bodies use the operation worker pool.

docs.title: collect(vals)
docs.text: Return one Val containing all results in input order. Callback aggregation waits for every member to settle and reports the first failure in list order. It does not allocate a blocking worker per member.

docs.title: force(x, timeout=None)
docs.text: Materialize a value or handle after the relevant guards allow publication. A rejected world raises Squashed; a surviving failure propagates. This blocks the tracer where a concrete result is required.

docs.title: choose(pool, by, k=1, hint=None, predict_losers=None, bound=None)
docs.text:
Select k ranked members using a concrete or asynchronous ranking of pool indices. Return a list of rank-specific Choice handles. Rankings must contain distinct, valid integer positions and enough members for k; duplicate pool members are invalid.

hint carries per-member scheduling information. predict_losers can demote speculative work without removing its surviving execution obligation. bound introduces the distinct bound-commit algorithm.

docs.title: gate(x, cond)
docs.text: Keep x when the condition is true; otherwise squash it. Returns a Choice, with no false-case fallback value.

docs.title: loop(init, body, max_iters, lookahead=None)
docs.text: Call body(state) → (next_state, continue_condition) under successive entry guards. Return the state entering the first round whose condition is false, or the final next state if the bound is exhausted. See loop semantics.

docs.title: selection_bounds(pool, bounds, k=1)
docs.text: Open a bound-commit contest. bounds aligns with the flattened pool; None exempts a member. Attach each member's score with contest.attach(index, score_val), then pass bound=contest to a matching choose. Valid upper bounds and strict rival-score evidence are required.

docs.title: prefetch_on_stream(source, build, *, model="judge", chunk_tokens=None)
docs.text: Register advisory text-prefix cache warming for a transformed future prompt. Enabled only with speculation and SpecConfig.judge_prefetch, and requires the text wire. build(full_text_so_far) returns a prompt string or None; it must be fast and pure. Prefetch outputs are discarded.

docs.title: tool(fn, args=None, *, name="", effect="unknown", alpha=None, alpha_name="", after=None)
docs.text:
Register a tool body receiving one JSON argument dictionary. args=None means an empty dictionary. Nested values resolve before canonical argument hashing. effect is "unknown" or "speculable".

alpha declares a pure observation projection; alpha_name names it. after accepts a tool handle, value, or sequence of such predecessors and waits for their settlement without propagating their values or failures.

docs.title: obs(t, alpha=None, *, name="", alpha_name="")
docs.text: Return a Seq containing a late-bound named observation segment. Its bytes are supplied only when the projection image is materialized.

docs.title: observe(t, alpha=None, *, name="", alpha_name="")
docs.text: Return the structured projected image as a Val. Use this for Python computation on the declared observation.

docs.title: ack(t)
docs.text: Return Val[None] when the body finishes, propagating its failure without reading the observation.

docs.title: expect(t, guess, *, alpha=None, name="", alpha_name="")
docs.text: Return a hit/miss Choice: the guessed string on exact image equality, or a real-observation hole on mismatch. Both surviving paths preserve the declared observation bytes.

docs.title: classify(t, cases, *, alpha=None, alpha_name="", name="")
docs.text: Route exact projected image strings to already-constructed branch values. cases is a closed mapping. An observation outside it is a projection error.

docs.title: calls(y)
docs.text: Expose the prefix-stable ProjectedCalls interface of a generated Seq that was created with a prepared tool-stream projection. It is for custom streamed tool control, not for parsing arbitrary generated text after the fact. See tool_projection in the canonical tools module and streaming design.

docs.title: ToolDef(fn, effect="unknown", ..., obs=..., guess=..., description=None, input_schema=None)
docs.text:
Configure one named tool in the infer(..., tools={name: definition}) registry. input_schema describes only the arguments, without a provider function wrapper. description defaults to the callable's first docstring line, with the mapping key as the neutral fallback.

Omitting both the observation contract and guess enables the default exact policy and draft predictor. Explicit obs=Exact() or guess=None suppresses the implicit predictor. The older policy= spelling is accepted, but supplying it together with obs= is an error.

docs.title: Observation policy types
docs.text:
Export Contract Policy Conservative protocol base: exact image through a real-result hole; shallow call-local sessions Exact() Select guesses only on exact equality; otherwise use the real image Ignore(text="done") Constant observation without reading the result Project(alpha) Pure reduction before exact observation selection Enum(cases, by=...) Ordered declared representatives selected through the classifier hole() A placeholder filled by the real image open() Alias of hole(); distinct from Python's file-opening built-in

For custom new_session, project, slots, and select, read policy execution.

docs.title: Runtime and diagnostics
docs.text:
Export Purpose make_runtime(...) Construct local main and optional judge engines make_remote_runtime(...) Construct a certified remote token-wire runtime EngineSpec Declare the local model, capacity, engine arguments, parser, and drafter ModelSpec Bind a role to an engine specification and chat template settings Runtime Own engines, tracing contexts, scheduler, worker pools, and ledgers SpecConfig Configure branch speculation and advisory policies render_timeline(panels, out_path, *, title="") Write a standalone SVG from one or more timeline panels Squashed Exception signaling that the requested world was rejected

See runtime configuration for constructors, defaults, and lifecycle methods. Import TimelinePanel from agentir.diagnostics.viz.

docs.title: Canonical advanced modules
docs.text:
agentir.compile provides shape_trace, StaticGraph, GraphBreak, and plan types. agentir.tracing.tools provides tool_projection and the compatibility infer_tools function. Adapter-specific remote and judge-server types live under agentir.execution.

Although infer_tools, tool_projection, and TimelinePanel remain root attributes for compatibility, they are not in the supported root __all__ surface. New examples use their canonical modules or infer(..., tools=...).

Source: root exports, DSL implementation, and tool definitions.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Installing AgentIR adds the agentir command. Run agentir --help or agentir COMMAND --help for the parser's complete option list. The CLI uses the local model runtime; certified remote and Harbor workflows have their own Python and Harbor entry points.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose Model required? agentir list Print registered algorithms and tasks No agentir warm Load and handshake the configured engine, then close it Yes agentir bench Run a dataset slice and report measurements Yes agentir refdiff Compare guarded lowering with the serial reference Yes agentir check Require both reference and scheduler differentials Yes

Static compilation is available through agentir.compile.shape_trace, not a CLI subcommand.

docs.title: Engine options
docs.text:
All model-executing commands require --model. Common options include --judge-model, --devices, --judge-devices, --judge-process, --max-model-len, --gpu-mem, --judge-gpu-mem, --max-inflight (32), and --wire (text).

The CLI's --judge-process controls the dedicated scoring-server path. Token-wire and model compatibility still follow the runtime restrictions.

docs.title: Benchmark options
docs.text:
bench requires --task and --algo:

Option Default Meaning --task Required gsm8k, math500, aime2024, or amc2023 --algo Required One of the eight built-in algorithms --n 10 Number of problems --offset 0 Starting position in the dataset --concurrency 1 Problems in flight --spec on on, off, both, ladder, or fastbase --out Unset JSONL run record path --dump-ledger DIR Unset Per-problem ledger output directory --runtime-graph [DIR] Unset Timeline output; optional value selects a directory

Datasets are cached under ~/.cache/agentir. First access can download source data. both uses a fixed off-then-on order; ladder adds serial and oracle arms. fastbase runs a phase-alternating baseline, guarded speculation-off, and guarded speculation-on as three arms. The phase arm enables phase_serial; inspect the recorded algorithm configuration when comparing it with other arms.

docs.title: Speculation options
docs.text:
--window 2 and --spec-inflight 8 set the depth and budget. Optional flags include --depth1-unmetered, --judge-prefetch, --ev-gate, and --spec-preempt. --prune-margin configures the beam predictor where supported.

These flags address different mechanisms; see prediction and optimization before enabling several together.

docs.title: Algorithm options
docs.text:
Option Default Typical use --k 6 Candidate count for sampling algorithms --width, --branch, --rounds 2, 2, 3 Beam shape --iters 4 Refinement or MCTS iteration bound --step-tokens 160 Per-step or rollout budget --late-step-tokens Unset Optional later-step budget --early-steps 3 Steps before the later budget takes effect --step-stop Unset Step delimiter --max-tokens 512 Main output budget --judge-tokens 96 Judge generation budget --scorer logprob logprob, judge, or prm --prm-agg min min, last, mean, or prod --temperature, --top-p 0.8, 0.95 Sampling settings --run-seed 20260708 Runtime seed

--no-explain disables self-consistency's explanation. --chat uses chat-formatted prompting. --phase-serial introduces algorithm phase barriers. --bound-commit requires the supported scoring and step-boundary conditions; it changes the early-stopping contract in both arms.

Options are dispatched according to the selected algorithm, so a shared parser option is not evidence that every algorithm uses it.

docs.title: Check options and exit status
docs.text:
check defaults to --task gsm8k --algo beam_search; refdiff defaults to --task gsm8k --algo best_of_n. Both accept --offset. check --runtime-graph [PATH] renders the compared runs, and --slow-tool-audit additionally repeats declared-speculable tools for an observation audit.

Successful checks exit zero. Semantic mismatches and setup failures exit nonzero. Automation should check the process status and preserve the report, not infer success from the existence of an output file.

Source: cli.py.

docs.title: Runtime configuration
docs.text: These are the defaults in the checked-in AgentIR 1.3.0 implementation. Algorithm functions and CLI flags may override generation defaults; always inspect the effective settings of the entry point you use.

docs.title: Local runtime
docs.text:
make_runtime takes keyword-only arguments:

Argument Default Meaning model Required Main model identifier engine_args None Additional validated vLLM engine configuration devices None Main engine GPU visibility judge_model None Separate judge model; otherwise judge aliases main judge_engine_args, judge_devices None Judge-specific configuration judge_process False Managed separate judge-server process, text wire only judge_server_attach None Attach a judge-server endpoint instead of spawning it max_inflight 32 Per-engine AgentIR request capacity spec None Use the SpecConfig defaults below run_seed 20260708 Root seed for invocation and node seed derivation default_params None Override default generation parameters wire "text" "text" or "tokens" event_granularity "auto" Event observation policy chat_template_kwargs None Main chat-template options judge_chat_template_kwargs None Inherit main options; explicit {} resets them

EngineSpec also exposes scheduling_policy="priority", enable_prefix_caching=True, reasoning_parser="auto", expected_version="0.24.0", and optional vllm_token_drafter. Its resolved physical configuration determines engine sharing.

docs.title: Remote runtime
docs.text:
make_remote_runtime requires model and base_url, with the following additional options:

Argument Default Meaning api_key, headers None Request authentication and headers expected_version "0.24.0" Required vLLM version; None removes only this version pin certificate_mode "required" Required Tier-1 contract expected_certificate_sha256 None Optional exact certificate pin request_timeout 900.0 HTTP request timeout in seconds render_cache_entries 128 Successful-render cache capacity thinking_token_budget None Optional supported server reasoning budget chat_template_kwargs None Certified rendering options

max_inflight, spec, run_seed, and default_params have the same defaults as the local helper. The remote helper fixes the wire to tokens. Read remote execution for endpoint and capability requirements.

docs.title: Speculation configuration
docs.text:
SpecConfig field Default Meaning enabled True Enable branch speculation window 2 Maximum eligible unresolved guard depth max_spec_inflight 8 Speculative request budget depth1_unmetered False Exempt depth-one work from that budget loop_lookahead None Reserved configuration field; current loop reads its own lookahead argument or derives its default from window decision_timeout 600.0 Seconds before an unresolved decision fails; None disables the watchdog op_drain_timeout 600.0 Seconds allowed for effect-obligation draining engine_restart_limit 1 Physical engine recovery limit judge_prefetch False Enable speculative prefix warming prefetch_chunk_tokens 64 Minimum new source tokens between warm requests prefetch_max_inflight 2 Dedicated prefetch lane capacity per engine static_plan None Compiled per-decision funding plan ev_gate False Fund speculation using estimated expected value ev_gate_p_floor 0.05 Cold-start probability floor for EV funding spec_preempt False Permit strictly better speculation to reclaim eligible slots

window and max_spec_inflight do not replace max_inflight; physical capacity remains an independent limit. Turning speculation off also disables speculative prefix warming.

docs.title: Sampling parameters
docs.text:
The runtime's base defaults are max_tokens=512, temperature=0.8, and top_p=0.95. The autonomous tool loop defaults to temperature zero unless overridden.

The public parameter whitelist contains:

max_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, logit_bias,
stop, stop_token_ids, repetition_penalty, frequency_penalty,
presence_penalty, logprob_topk, skip_special_tokens,
include_stop_str_in_output, structured

Arbitrary vLLM sampling kwargs are not accepted. Parameters are copied into a canonical frozen representation before hashing. The DSL derives the seed and does not accept it as an ordinary sampling argument.

structured must specify exactly one of json, regex, choice, grammar, json_object, or structural_tag. Availability also depends on adapter capabilities. Token drafting rejects min_p and logit_bias by key presence, even if supplied as zero or an empty mapping.

docs.title: Lifecycle methods
docs.text:
Method Behavior run(fn, *args, problem_key="p0", invocation_key=None, **kwargs) Run a fresh tracing context, return its result, and drain effect obligations submit(fn, *args, ..., **kwargs) Return a concurrent future for lower-level asynchronous orchestration warm(timeout=3600.0) Load and handshake configured engines chat_prefix(messages, *, role="main", tools=None, generation=None, add_generation_prompt=True, timeout=600.0) Render with the selected engine's template ledger_for(problem_key) Return engine ledger rows for the label events_for(problem_key) Return recorded runtime events for the label close() Release runtime-owned threads, pools, and engines

For custom construction, Runtime(models, ...) takes a role-to-ModelSpec mapping and optional role aliases. It defaults to 32 operation workers and 16 tracer workers. Nested invocations must leave enough workers for children to make progress; the subagent example documents that case.

Source: runtime.py, engine.py, and parameter validation.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Term Meaning Agent branch speculation Executing possible agent continuations before a selection decides which survive Attempt One physical execution of a logical engine request; retries create new attempts Bound commit Algorithmic truncation after strict rival-score evidence proves a candidate cannot enter the selected top-k Choice A symbolic handle for one rank of an unresolved selection Commitment Permission for completed work to belong to the surviving computation Control plane Python operations and decisions that coordinate model and tool work Data dependency Input content that must exist before a request can be constructed or issued Decision A ranked selection or boolean gate with an entry guard DrawId A sampling occurrence identified by call site, scoped occurrence, and expansion lane Engine node / E-node A logical model request with a frozen prompt descriptor and observation contract Epoch An engine generation used to fence stale attempts and events across recovery Guard A conjunction of conditions under which a node survives Hoisting Rewriting a continuation of a choice into guarded continuations of its possible members Hole A declared observation slot filled by the real projected tool result IR Intermediate representation: the graph and symbolic values between the Python program and execution Invocation One execution of a program in a fresh tracing context Ledger Per-node records of registration, issue, completion, guard timing, and disposition NodeId Content-addressed identity of a logical request, independent of its physical attempt Observation image The string or canonical JSON representation exposed by a tool's declared projection Observation policy A tool contract that projects results, declares candidates, and selects among them Prefix caching Engine reuse of computation for matching prompt-token prefixes Projection A pure, named view of a tool result, or a declared interpretation of streamed model output Seq An opaque symbolic prompt state, including prior prompt segments and generated output Speculable effect A declaration that extra tool executions and retries are safe under the intended observation contract Spine Canonical sequence of Lit, Out, and Obs segments that describes a prompt Squash Reject a world and cancel its active work without publishing its result Static shape A symbolic graph of possible program structure, with loop bodies and dynamic holes Tier-1 The implemented certified remote render / token-in-token-out / derender protocol Token drafting Engine-level candidate-token generation followed by token verification Tool node / T-node A logical tool body identified by name, canonical arguments, draw, and effect contract Unknown effect A conservative contract that fences body execution until its world is committed Val An asynchronous Python value carrying dependency and guard information Weak control dependency A keep-or-cancel condition that does not supply request input bytes Window The eligible unresolved guard depth for speculative issue Wire The representation of prompt atoms: strings or exact token-ID tuples World One combination of selection outcomes under which a handle instance exists

Return to architecture to see these terms in one execution, or the API to find the corresponding operations.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start by locating the boundary that failed: package import, engine startup, graph construction, decision resolution, tool parsing, or result comparison. Preserve the smallest program and the effective configuration that reproduce it.

docs.title: Installation and engine startup
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause Next action agentir cannot be imported Wrong environment or missing editable installation Run python -m pip install -e . in the environment executing the program vLLM is unavailable Only the base package is installed Install the local engine extra, or use a certified remote runtime Engine subprocess repeatedly starts Runtime created at module import time Move creation behind if __name__ == "__main__": Out-of-memory during startup or generation Model, context, or concurrent KV state exceeds capacity Reduce the applicable context/concurrency settings and verify device placement Version or capability handshake fails Adapter and engine contract differ Check the pinned version and required parser/rendering capabilities

The base package deliberately imports vLLM lazily. agentir list succeeding establishes that the package loads; it does not validate a GPU runtime.

docs.title: Symbolic values and control flow
docs.text:
A handle cannot be used as a Python boolean. Use gate, choose, or loop for symbolic control. If the next program fragment truly depends on inspecting concrete data, call force deliberately and accept the barrier.

cat rejects independent choices. The current lowering supports one independent unresolved choice in a composition. Reduce the combination to one decision or materialize one selection before combining them.

The result contains the prompt. text(seq) reads the full state. Use out_text(seq) to read the generation tail.

The loop returns an older state than expected. On a false continue condition, loop returns the state that entered that round. Put acceptance/rejection logic around that contract; see the loop example.

GraphBreak occurs during shape tracing. This describes a static compiler boundary, not necessarily a runtime-invalid program. Read the reported source location and supported shape behavior.

docs.title: Decisions and cancellation
docs.text:
Squashed reaches force. You attempted to publish a rejected world. Check whether a false gate needs an explicit alternative or whether a losing handle escaped its intended branch.

A ranking is rejected. Return distinct integer pool indices, not scores, booleans, duplicate indices, or newly created sequence handles. Provide enough ranked members for k.

An invocation waits on a decision. Check whether its ranking operation can complete, whether you created an external wait cycle, and whether the decision watchdog is enabled. A guard cannot replace missing data.

A cancelled tool still finishes. A running Python body may be impossible to stop. The effect declaration controls whether that body was allowed to start; cancellation does not undo it.

docs.title: Tools and remote execution
docs.text:
Symptom Check Tool loop rejects the runtime It requires the token wire and a supported tool-capable family Tool callable reports argument mismatch It receives one dictionary, not unpacked keyword arguments Tool schema is rejected Pass the argument JSON Schema without the provider function wrapper Unexpected predictor generations appear ToolDef(fn) implicitly enables the default predictor; explicit obs=Exact() or guess=None disables it Projection or selector error Projection must be pure; selection must return a declared slot; a custom policy error is not an ordinary miss State leaks between policy calls Override new_session if nested mutable state must be call-local Remote certificate route is missing Install and enable AgentIR's middleware on the server Remote instance or digest mismatch Re-establish the certified deployment contract; do not reuse assumptions across server instances Remote calls arrive only after generation ends This is the current terminal derender boundary, not local incremental dispatch Two token-wire engines are rejected Verify complete tokenizer compatibility, including special tokens

ProjectionDivergence means a stream or replay disagreed with an already-established observation contract. Retrying with a different parser to suppress it can change semantics; first identify the mismatched model, template, parser, or call prefix.

docs.title: Correct but slower
docs.text:
Inspect a timeline before increasing the window. A larger window can issue more losing work, displace useful requests, and consume more KV memory. A tiny decision latency may leave no overlap to recover.

Remote rendering costs, terminal-only call publication, expensive predictors, and low cache hit rates can also dominate. Change one setting at a time and preserve the same task, algorithm, and observation contract.

docs.title: Report a reproducible issue
docs.text: Include a minimal program, AgentIR and engine versions, model/parser/template settings, wire, SpecConfig, the relevant traceback, and a small ledger or check report. Include the failing test or command and whether the failure occurs with speculation off. For authenticated remote deployments, redact credentials from any shared configuration.

docs.title: Benchmarking
docs.text: A useful benchmark states which optimization changed, confirms that the compared programs are equivalent under their contracts, and measures the workload at its intended concurrency. Keep those questions separate.

docs.title: Start with a paired smoke run
docs.text:
After passing correctness checks, run a small comparison:

agentir bench \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --task gsm8k --algo heavy --n 3 \
  --spec both --concurrency 1 \
  --out runs/heavy-smoke.jsonl \
  --dump-ledger runs/heavy-ledgers \
  --runtime-graph runs/heavy-timelines

The output JSONL contains run metadata, summaries, and per-problem result records. The example is a smoke experiment; three problems do not support a general speedup claim.

The CLI's both mode runs off and then on in a fixed order with the same run seed. It is convenient for diagnosis, but it is not a randomized crossover design. Formal paired launchers in the repository implement their own declared ordering and validation.

docs.title: Hold the program fixed
docs.text:
Record the model and tokenizer revisions, engine version and arguments, chat template and parser configuration, sampling parameters, algorithm knobs, task slice, seed and invocation scoping, speculation settings, and concurrency.

For tools, also record the effect declaration, observation projection, prediction policy, and remote certificate. A narrower observation image can change the agent's information; it is not merely a faster implementation of the same full-observation program.

If you test vLLM drafting, distinguish it from AgentIR branch speculation. A factorial comparison can vary both explicitly; a single ambiguous “spec on” label cannot explain which treatment produced the result.

docs.title: Choose the unit of comparison
docs.text:
Question Appropriate profile Does one task finish sooner? Paired task latency at concurrency 1 Does a loaded service finish more tasks? Fixed higher-concurrency throughput profile Is time traded for extra generation? Committed and wasted tokens, request counts, and engine time Does task quality remain acceptable? Paired correctness or task success with a declared margin

Do not mix per-request latency, per-task latency, and total suite makespan. In agent programs, one task can contain many overlapping engine requests and tool calls.

Warmup, model loading, dataset download, and steady-state execution are different phases. State which are included in reported timing. A fast warm cache is not evidence for a cold-start workload.

docs.title: Understand the ablation ladder
docs.text:
--spec ladder exposes four diagnostic levels:

Arm Interpretation A0 Serial source execution A1 Guarded graph execution with branch speculation off A2 Guarded graph execution with branch speculation on A3 Oracle decision replay, removing decision latency from the replayed path

A0 to A1 can expose concurrency obtained from graph execution itself. A1 to A2 isolates branch speculation within that setup. The oracle is a diagnostic counterfactual with recorded decisions, not a deployable serving algorithm.

docs.title: Summarize paired data carefully
docs.text:
The statistical helpers support paired log-latency summaries, task-cluster bootstrap intervals, paired sign-flip tests, and Holm correction. Tasks, rather than repeated attempts treated as independent tasks, are the aggregation unit in the formal analyses.

The sign-flip implementation enumerates assignments for at most 16 units and otherwise uses Monte Carlo with a plus-one correction. Quality non-inferiority requires its lower confidence bound to exceed the negative declared margin. An insignificant quality difference alone is not proof of non-inferiority.

Choose the analysis before inspecting results. Report exclusions and missing measurements, retain the raw records, and tie summaries to the exact configuration and artifact hashes used to produce them.

docs.title: Use formal scripts with their locks
docs.text:
The repository has several generations of experiment scripts, from small tool-loop studies to remote Terminal-Bench and ordinary token-drafting studies. Some launchers contain fixed cluster paths and frozen eligibility rules. Read the relevant experiment family before adapting one.

This manual explains the measurement machinery. It does not turn historical notes, preregistrations, or incomplete artifact references into a new verified performance result.

Source: runner.py, stats.py, and tasks.py.

docs.title: Correctness checks
docs.text: Before asking whether speculation is faster, establish that the same logical program survives. AgentIR provides two complementary checks: one for the tracer's lowering, and one for speculation-on versus speculation-off scheduling.

docs.title: The two gates
docs.text:
Gate Comparison What it tests A: reference differential Guarded speculation-off execution versus an independent serial source interpreter Whether guarded lowering preserves source-level selection and effects B: scheduler differential A captured off arm versus a fresh speculation-on runtime Whether speculative scheduling preserves the committed computation

agentir refdiff runs the reference differential. agentir check requires both gates to pass. A failed check exits nonzero; a fast run with a failed gate is not valid performance evidence.

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
With a working engine installation:

agentir refdiff \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --algo best_of_n --task gsm8k --offset 0

agentir check \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --algo beam_search --task gsm8k --offset 0 \
  --runtime-graph check.svg

These commands load a model and may fetch the selected dataset into the task cache. Use a model and engine capacity suitable for the algorithm. The SVG shows the compared runtime schedules on a shared time scale.

docs.title: Why a serial interpreter is necessary
docs.text:
Turning speculation off still uses guarded lowering. If the tracer constructs the wrong graph, both on and off arms could agree on the same bug.

The serial interpreter instead follows decisions before constructing their selected continuation. It shares canonical identity construction with the runtime, but does not use the speculative hoisting execution path. Comparing the two checks that they identify the same surviving work.

Gate A records engine outputs from the guarded arm and replays them through the serial interpreter. This isolates lowering correctness from engine nondeterminism. Missing replay entries fail closed.

docs.title: What the scheduler comparison observes
docs.text:
Gate B uses a fresh speculation-on runtime and checks committed identities, prompt/output atoms and text, final results, failure behavior, and tool semantics against the captured off arm. Request-attempt histories may differ; the committed computation must still satisfy the comparison contract.

Tool bodies are recorded in the first arm and replayed in the comparison arm. There is no fallback that quietly executes an unrecorded effect. This avoids repeating unknown effects merely to perform a differential check.

Replay establishes a controlled semantic comparison. It does not establish that a changing external tool would return the same result when invoked again, or that seed equality alone guarantees bitwise engine reproducibility on every platform.

docs.title: Audit declared-speculable tools
docs.text:
agentir check --slow-tool-audit additionally re-executes completed tools declared effect="speculable" and compares exact observation-image bytes. Unknown-effect tools are never rerun by this audit.

The audit deliberately repeats declared-safe executions. A mismatch can reveal an unstable projection, hidden state, or an invalid speculability declaration. Use the normal record/replay check when you only need the lowering and scheduling comparison.

docs.title: Account for algorithmic truncation
docs.text:
With a valid bound-commit algorithm, losing candidates can end at different permitted prefixes. Diagnostics distinguish that permitted truncation from changed surviving bytes. The same bound rule must be enabled in both arms, and the proof must ensure those truncated bytes do not affect a surviving result.

Read score-bound truncation before treating a prefix difference as harmless.

docs.title: Tests and real-engine evidence
docs.text:
The test suite includes deterministic fake engines and HTTP fixtures for ordering, retries, identities, protocol failures, and graph behavior. These make edge cases reproducible without a GPU. Other tests and scripts exercise real vLLM capabilities.

A passing engine-independent suite does not replace an integration run on the actual model, parser, and server configuration. Record which checks ran and which engine-dependent checks were unavailable.

Source: reference.py, tool_audit.py, and CLI gate tests.

docs.title: Timelines and diagnostics
docs.text: A timeline explains where an invocation waited, what ran early, and which work survived. Start with one problem before aggregating a benchmark: a wall-time number alone cannot show whether the expected overlap occurred.

docs.title: Render a runtime ledger
docs.text:
After runtime.run(program, problem_key="example"), while the runtime is available:

from agentir import render_timeline
from agentir.diagnostics.viz import TimelinePanel

rows = runtime.ledger_for("example")
render_timeline(
    TimelinePanel(label="Speculation on", rows=rows),
    "timeline.svg",
    title="One AgentIR invocation",
)

render_timeline writes a standalone SVG without a plotting dependency. TimelinePanel is imported from its canonical diagnostics module. Supply a sequence of panels to compare runs on a shared time scale; optional runtime events add operation and decision lanes.

For CLI runs, --runtime-graph writes timelines and --dump-ledger DIR saves per-problem ledger JSON. See the CLI reference.

docs.title: Read the timestamps in order
docs.text:
Ledger field Meaning A long gap can indicate t_reg Node registered in the graph The tracer has exposed possible work t_data_ready Required input data became available Upstream generation, an operation, or observation is still needed t_issue Physical request issued Funding, priority, or engine capacity delayed ready work t_first First observed engine output event Prefill or engine queueing; interpret with event granularity t_done Request finished Generation or service time t_guard_resolved Keep-or-cancel condition resolved Selection or loop decision latency

Some records are registered but never issued, and some adapters expose only terminal semantic events. Do not treat absent or terminal-only first-event timing as a measured first-token latency.

docs.title: Separate execution from usefulness
docs.text:
speculative says how the request was issued. disposition says what happened to its work:

  • committed: part of the surviving computation.
  • wasted: executed or registered in a rejected world.
  • failed: ended in a relevant failure.

A request can be issued speculatively and later commit. It can also complete early and then be discarded. Count useful lead separately from total speculative work.

cached_tokens reports engine-observed cached prompt tokens. A value of zero means no reported cache hit; -1 means the information was unavailable. Neither a shared symbolic prefix nor fork_parent alone proves a physical cache hit.

docs.title: Diagnose a disappointing run
docs.text:
Observation Inspect next No speculative requests issued Whether the decision resolved before input data; window and budget settings Ready work waits while the engine is full Committed load, per-engine capacity, and speculative interference Most speculative tokens are wasted Candidate count, guard depth, decision quality, and predictor hit rate Correct predictions save little time Tool latency, remote terminal boundary, render cost, and continuation length A large lead sum produces little wall-time gain Overlapping leads, resource contention, and other critical-path work Cache metrics disappear Engine capability and telemetry coverage, not just prefix construction

The summed interval between speculative issue and guard resolution is a lead metric. Multiple requests can accumulate lead over the same wall-clock interval. Do not report that sum as elapsed time saved.

docs.title: Use telemetry for the right question
docs.text:
bench.gpu_telemetry samples GPU metrics and validates the coverage of its output. bench.vllm_metrics_telemetry captures server metrics, including scheduler and KV-cache observations where available. Experiment scripts preserve raw samples and generate checked summaries.

Low GPU utilization or apparent request underfill can be useful signals, but they are proxies. They do not by themselves prove an engine “bubble,” explain causality, or attribute a slowdown to one policy.

Continue with benchmarking to turn individual traces into a controlled comparison.

docs.title: Experiment archive
docs.text: This page maps research records and launchers to the question they study. These files preserve experimental contracts and historical context. Use the rest of the manual for the current public programming interface.

docs.title: Agent branch search
docs.text:
The hephaestus_beam_spec_* launchers cover beam-search pairing, ablation ladders, uniform policies, and multi-GPU layouts. analyze_beam_spec_paired.py validates and summarizes paired artifacts. Older bench_v12_* and bench_fasttts.sh scripts describe earlier sweep profiles.

scripts/baselines/README.md documents the ordinary asyncio best-of-N baseline. It calls a serving endpoint directly and is useful for separating graph-runtime effects from agent algorithm choice.

docs.title: Tools and observation prediction
docs.text:
The original paired tools study, diverse tool study, and drafting extension have distinct drivers:

Driver Focus bench_tools_paired.py Paired observation-policy and speculation behavior bench_tools_diverse_paired.py A broader tool workload bench_tools_diverse_drafting.py Observation drafting on the diverse suite check_tools.py Tool correctness checks bench_p05_predict.py Predictor-focused experiments

Their frozen English preregistrations remain in the repository: original tools study, diverse study, and terminal-latency study.

docs.title: Harbor and terminal agents
docs.text:
terminal_bench_formal_lock.json binds the formal Terminal-Bench setup. The paired launcher records endpoint, certificate, environment, model, and resource evidence; analyze_terminal_bench_paired.py checks those contracts before summarizing.

The terminal-drafter coordinator and analyze_terminal_drafter.py add a separate token-drafting treatment with strict certificate and execution-configuration matching. bench.terminal_drafter_evidence supplies shared evidence validation.

Latency-only summaries in analyze_terminal_latency.py answer a narrower question. A successful artifact parse does not automatically establish task-quality validity or a completed formal trial.

docs.title: Ordinary token drafting
docs.text:
bench_ordinary_spec_generation.py studies ordinary model generation with engine token drafting. It is not an AgentIR DSL branch-speculation workload.

The family includes workload construction, model-cache preflight, vLLM configuration resolution, server lifecycle management, startup validation, reference-equivalence production, paired analysis, and bundle finalization. The lock files distinguish a formal MATH500 latency profile at concurrency 1 from descriptive higher-concurrency profiles such as C8 and C32.

Read the exact lock and analyzer version together. Later evidence gates supersede some older workflows; mixing artifact generations can produce invalid comparisons.

docs.title: Mechanism demonstrations
docs.text:
examples/subagent_as_tool.py runs a child AgentIR invocation as a tool, alongside a predicted summary. The child has a restricted leaf-tool registry and does not recursively expose the delegate tool. It demonstrates nested runtime composition and prediction verification; it is not a general recursive-agent benchmark.

The Harmony and DeepSeek verification scripts exercise particular parser and model combinations. Cluster wrappers, environment JSON, and synchronization scripts support those deployments and are not required by the base package.

docs.title: Reuse a study responsibly
docs.text:
Read its frozen protocol, locate the raw artifacts, validate provenance and coverage, and run its analyzer before interpreting a result. Preserve the original locks when designing a new variant; create a separately named protocol and output bundle instead.

The source map links the implementation families and their tests.
